summary: The first source-owned omission is dig.c:digactualhole() when downward digging selects HOLE. The C path calls maketrap(), whose HOLE branch calls hole_destination() and consumes rn2(4), then continues through the hero fall and level-arrival effects. JavaScript digactualhole() records an unported gap and returns for every trap type other than PIT before calling maketrap(). Port the whole digactualhole() function and preserve its existing callers; hole_destination() itself already matches the C loop.

source.branch: The v26 recipe gives a Wizard a wand of digging and aims it down from a diggable floor square. C zap_dig() takes its downward, non-stairway branch and calls dighole(FALSE, TRUE, NULL); on this ordinary floor, dighole() selects HOLE and calls digactualhole(..., BY_YOU, HOLE). In the recorded run the hero falls through, so the hero HOLE branch reaches goto_level() and spoteffects().
callers: C: dig.c:zap_dig() (1604-1607) calls dighole(FALSE, TRUE, NULL); dighole() (885-1023), after its ordinary-room path selects HOLE, calls digactualhole(..., BY_YOU, HOLE) at 1016-1019. JavaScript follows js/zap.js:zap_dig() (6087-6088) -> js/dig.js:dighole() (1618-1626) -> js/dig.js:digactualhole(); the last function currently returns at its non-PIT guard.

C: apply.c:do_break_wand() (4071-4072) also calls digactualhole(..., BY_OBJECT, PIT-or-HOLE). JavaScript js/apply.js:do_break_wand() currently records this non-hero branch as unported around 4760; a whole-function port must preserve this production caller.
C: dig.c:dig() (374) calls dighole(FALSE, FALSE, NULL) from the downward digging occupation, which can reach the same HOLE arm. JavaScript js/dig.js already calls dighole() from the occupation path.
dependencies: trap.c:maketrap() returns the trap consumed by digactualhole(); its HOLE arm calls hole_destination(), which uses dng_bottom(). The existing JavaScript path is js/trap.js:hole_destination() and maketrap().

do.c:goto_level() and hack.c:spoteffects() perform the hero-fall transition and arrival effects from digactualhole(); existing JavaScript implementations are js/do.js:goto_level() and js/hack.js:spoteffects().

The remaining whole-function branches also consult shk.c:shopdig()/pay_for_damage(), dokick.c:impact_drop(), pickup.c:pickup(), trap.c:mintrap(), teleport.c:teleport_pet(), dungeon.c:get_level(), and dog.c:migrate_to_level(). Preserve result-used calls and record only permitted discarded-result gaps.

evidence: The saved queue entry .cache/v26-digging-down-queue-entry.json and evaluation challenges/evaluations/20261007095608-v26.json identify the first mismatch at segment 0, step 31, key >: C logs rn2(4)=1 at hole_destination(trap.c:450), while JavaScript has rn2(19)=13 at that aligned RNG position; the screen and cursor diverge at the same step. The C recording then displays “You dig a hole through the floor. You fall through...”.

The independent recipe challenges/cases/v26/v26-digging-down.recipe.session.json sets a Wizard with a wand of digging and sends z, o, > after wishing for the wand. The recorded case has 41 steps; this is the down-wand route, not a pit-occupation input.

C source nethack-c/upstream/src/dig.c:1548-1607 routes a downward, non-stairway zap through dighole(FALSE, TRUE, NULL). In dig.c:1000-1019, an ordinary diggable room whose fillholetyp() is ROOM and whose checks do not require a pit reaches digactualhole(..., BY_YOU, HOLE).

C source nethack-c/upstream/src/dig.c:640-829 shows the whole digactualhole() contract. It calls maketrap() at 690, then the HOLE branch at 753-794 switches terrain, checks levitation/flying and the pet leash, and on a fall prints the message, advances one level with goto_level(), and runs spoteffects().

C source nethack-c/upstream/src/trap.c:519-523 calls hole_destination() when maketrap() receives a hole; hole_destination() increments the destination and calls rn2(4) at 448-451. JavaScript js/trap.js has this same loop at 568-581 and calls it from maketrap() at 962, so the missing RNG call comes from the caller never reaching maketrap().

JavaScript js/dig.js:1313-1323 explicitly records note_unported for every non-PIT trap type or non-hero call and returns. Its dighole() calls digactualhole() for the HOLE result at 1618-1626, then proceeds to spot_checks(); this skips C trap creation and the hero descent. The source owner is therefore the partial digactualhole() implementation, not a divergence in hole_destination().

The goal kind is file-port because the C behavior is missing behind an explicit JavaScript gap. Scope the whole dig.c:digactualhole() function (640-829), including its existing PIT branch and other callers, then verify the down-zap route through zap_dig() and the BY_OBJECT route from apply.c:do_break_wand().
